symptom: (1) `alter microflow` with `insert after $X begin declare $Late Integer = 0; end;` and then `replace loop … with begin loop … set $Late = $Late + 1; … end;` passed check with a 'not predicted' note and failed at exec: 'the fragment has errors: variable 'Late' is not declared'. (2) A producer moved upstream — `create or modify` restating `$Code = call …` above the declare it followed, or the same as an alter insert+drop in either order — was refused 'the fragment declares $Code, which the microflow already has' (and, once past that, '$Code is still used by: log …; return $Code')
cause: Two variable verdicts of an alter block (and of the patch create or modify splices with, which is one) were still taken against the flow as stored: the fragment builder was seeded only with the stored flow's variables (storedVariables + the full build's entity types), so a later fragment could read but not `set` or member-access what an earlier operation declares; and checkFragmentScope refused a fragment declaring any variable a stored activity declares, at the moment it ran, before a later operation dropped that activity — while checkOutputUnused counted readers the inserted producer now feeds
file: mdl/executor/cmd_alter_flow.go (applyTo, fragmentBuilder, buildFragmentVars, noteFragment, checkOutputUnused, checkDeclaredUnclashed); mdl/executor/validate_flow_verdicts.go (alterFlowViolations)
fix: Each applied fragment's declared variables (with the types its builder resolved) seed later fragments' builders, in check's pre-build as in exec; the clash with a stored producer is judged once every operation is applied and skips one the block takes away (or whose loop it replaces); a stored or fragment reader of a removed output is no 'user' when another operation's fragment declares the variable upstream of it (declaredOnPath)
insight: 2f42df658 moved checkOutputUnused to the end of the block but left its two siblings per-operation; any check that answers 'does this variable exist' has to be judged against the flow the block writes, or create or modify's own diff (which turns a reorder into insert+drop) trips it. A useful corollary: a create-or-modify body that builds declares each variable once, so a 'declares $X, which the microflow already has' refusal from the splice is always false — the 1361 test pinned one as expected and now asserts the splice. Known order rule kept: a declaration by a LATER operation is not known to an earlier fragment (check reports it unpredicted, exec refuses it)
